G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
To our new Receptionist
On joining GLEUHR — handed over by the Front Desk Manager
Dear [Name],
Welcome to GLEUHR. I am writing to you directly because the role you have stepped into is the one a client meets first — and remembers longest. Long before anyone sees a doctor or a result, they form an opinion of this clinic in the first few seconds at your desk. That opinion is, in a real sense, the brand.
A receptionist at GLEUHR is not a person who answers a phone and hands over a form. You are the host of the branch. You greet every client by name within a few seconds, you make sure no enquiry is ever lost, you keep the desk and the data spotless, and you make every payment feel transparent and fair. When you do those things well, the whole visit starts and ends on warmth — and warmth is what brings people back.
I want to tell you how I think about this role. The smallest things are the whole job. A greeting in ten seconds. A callback returned the same day. A receipt sent to WhatsApp without being asked. A waiting client offered water before they have to look around for it. None of these is dramatic, but a hundred of them held every day is what separates a branch people recommend from one they merely tolerate. Take pride in the small things; they are not small to the client.
You report to the Front Desk Manager, who runs the operations and experience of the branch and who handed you this letter. The FDM is your daily guide — your huddle, your scorecard, the person you take a complaint or a long wait to. When a client has a clinical question, you route it to the doctor through the FDM; you never advise on clinical matters yourself. And there is one rule with no exceptions: you never take an off-system or cash-in-hand payment, and you never mishandle a client's data. Those are the lines that protect the client, the branch and you.
Your training takes six to eight days at our Chandigarh branch — three in the classroom and the rest live at the desk. You will be signed off when you can run the front desk solo for two to three consecutive days — greeting, bookings, calls, hospitality, billing and end-of-day — with the trainer watching from a step back. Not before.
Here is what you can expect from us. You will be taught properly before you are left alone at the desk. Your FDM and Senior Receptionist are there to support you, and asking when you are unsure is always the right move.
Here is what we ask from you. Greet every single client with genuine warmth, even at the end of a long day. Never let an enquiry slip. Be honest about a mistake before it becomes a problem. Treat every client's information and money with absolute care. And carry yourself, at the desk, as the face of a brand you are proud of.
Learn carefully over these days — what you build now becomes the way you run the desk for years. Make it count, and welcome to the team.
With respect, and with high expectations,
Urminder Singh
Founder & Managing Director  ·  Gleuhr Wellness Pvt Ltd
Handed over by the Front Desk Manager on Day 1 of joining. Accompanied by the KRA/KPI document and the training framework.
